app.eero_s_cloud_not_answering: eero's cloud is not answering. Local control still works — open it to find out where the connection stopped.
app_access.interface_password_not_your_e: This is the interface password, not your eero account.
app_access.least_8_characters_stored_onl: At least 8 characters. Stored only as a scrypt hash, and there is no recovery — losing it means deleting the data volume.
app_access.lost_docker: If you run it with Docker Compose
app_access.lost_docker_1: Delete the stored password, from the directory holding docker-compose.yml:
app_access.lost_docker_2: Restart the server so it re-reads its store:
app_access.lost_env_body: That variable wins over the stored hash, so deleting the file changes nothing. Set the variable to a new password, or unset it, and restart.
app_access.lost_intro: There is no reset link: the password is stored as a scrypt hash on the machine running this server, and nothing about your eero account can unlock it. Delete that one file, restart, and the interface asks you to choose a new password.
app_access.lost_nothing_else: Your eero sign-in is cleared too, so after choosing the new password you sign in to eero again. The node cache and every setting survive, and any browser still signed in here is signed out.
app_access.lost_reload: Reload this page. It will ask you to choose a new password.
app_access.lost_source: If you run it from source
app_access.passwords_do_not_match: Those two passwords do not match.
app_access.protects_interface_itself_any: This protects the interface itself. Anyone who can reach it can reboot your eeros, block clients, and see your Wi-Fi password, so it should not be left open on your network.

capabilities.what_eero_plus_is: eero Plus is a subscription service that adds enhanced security and privacy, ad blocking, parental controls, historical network insights, internet backup options, remote-access features, and bundled services like 1Password, Malwarebytes, and a VPN.
charts.short_window_hint: A window shorter than eero’s own reporting interval can come back empty even on a busy network — try a longer one.

client_detail.data_transferred_over_wind: Data transferred by this client over {window}
client_detail.dynamic_explained: Dynamic: handed out by DHCP and not guaranteed. The device may come back on a different address after a reboot or a long absence, which breaks anything pointed at this one.
client_detail.give_address_back_dhcp_poo: Give this address back to the DHCP pool
client_detail.high_retry_rate_usually_me: A high retry rate usually means interference or a congested channel rather than a weak signal.
client_detail.inferred_eero_from_device_: Inferred by eero from the device's MAC address and traffic, not reported by the device
client_detail.live_rates_waiting: eero publishes nothing until it is asked, so the first reading takes a few seconds to arrive.
client_detail.name: Name
client_detail.no_security_activity: Nothing recorded for this client in the last 7 days. eero counts these only while a device is on the network.
client_detail.no_usage_recorded_client: No usage recorded for this client.
client_detail.release_reservation_addr_n:
Release the reservation for {addr}?

{name} keeps its current address until the lease expires, then gets whatever the DHCP pool hands out — which may not be {addr}.{consequence}
client_detail.reserved_explained: Reserved: eero hands this device the same address every time, so a port forward or a firewall rule pointed at it keeps working after a reboot.
client_detail.security_privacy_hint: Requests this client made that eero inspected, and how many it blocked as a threat, an ad, or filtered content. Counted over the last 7 days.
client_detail.v6_global_hint: Reachable from the internet. A device using privacy extensions keeps a stable one and a temporary one that rotates, so two of these is normal.
client_detail.v6_link_hint: Valid only on the link it was seen on, and never routed. Every IPv6 interface has one; it is not usable as an address to reach the device.
client_detail.v6_ula_hint: Unique local address: reachable inside this network only, the IPv6 equivalent of a private address. eero hands these out whether or not the connection carries IPv6.
clients.no_clients_match_filter_offline: No clients match that filter. Offline clients are hidden by the Online filter, and blocked ones by every filter but Blocked.
clients.no_ipv4_lease_any_ipv6: No IPv4 lease. Any IPv6 addresses are in the device panel.

clients_by_band.mlo_clients.other: {count} Wi-Fi 7 clients are using more than one link at once.

ddns.eero_online_needs_plus: A name under eero.online is part of eero Plus. Every other provider in this list works without it.
ddns.eero_would_publish_note: eero has already reserved this name for your network. Nothing resolves to it until you connect.
ddns.gives_a_name_that_follows: A hostname that keeps pointing at this network when your provider changes its address.
ddns.ipv4_only: This provider updates IPv4 addresses only.
ddns.resolves_elsewhere: {name} points to {ip}, not to this network.
ddns_detail.no_session: Not updating: Eeronaut is not signed in to eero. Sign in, and tick "Stay signed in on this device" so updates carry on after a restart.
ddns_note.noip: On a free No-IP account a hostname has to be confirmed every 30 days from a link they email you, or it stops resolving. Updates from here will not keep it alive.
device_tree.switch_bridging: {count} devices arrive on port {port}, so something is bridging them onto it. eero cannot see the switch itself, which is why it has no name.

error_boundary.rest_interface_unaffected: The rest of the interface is unaffected. This usually means eero returned data in a shape this page did not expect, which is worth reporting.
filter_level.adult_id.desc: Nothing is filtered to start with. Turn on whichever filters you want.
filter_level.pre_k_id.desc: The tightest setting: only sites suitable for young children get through.
filter_level.pre_teen_id.desc: Blocks social media, messaging, and adult content, among other categories.
filter_level.teen_id.desc: Blocks adult, violent, and illegal content, and leaves the rest open.
filter_policy.block_illegal_content.desc: Sites that deal in illegal activity.
filter_policy.block_violent_content.desc: Sites centered on violence, weapons, or gore.
filter_policy.safe_search_enabled.desc: Makes search engines hide explicit results.
filter_policy.youtube_restricted.desc: Turns on YouTube's Restricted Mode, which hides videos marked as mature.
firmware.eero_will_not_start_one_now: eero will not start an update right now. It usually clears on its own within a few minutes.
firmware.install_now_confirm:
Install firmware {version} now?

Every eero restarts at once, so the whole network — including this page — goes down. A settings change takes five to eight minutes; a firmware install takes longer. Nothing on the network will have internet access until it comes back.
firmware.installed_automatically_at: It will be installed automatically between {time}.
firmware.installed_automatically_unknown: It will be installed automatically during {window}.
firmware.update_started: Update started. Every eero restarts; the network comes back in a few minutes.
inbound_access.address_outside_subnet: Choose an address inside this network's subnet.
inbound_access.check_external_port_range: Check the external port or range.
inbound_access.check_internal_port_range: Check the internal port or range.
inbound_access.confirm_disable_all.one: Disable {count} open rule? Anything relying on it will stop being reachable from the internet.
inbound_access.confirm_disable_all.other: Disable all {count} open rules? Anything relying on them will stop being reachable from the internet.
inbound_access.confirm_open_pinhole:
Open port {port} to {device} from the whole internet?

Unlike a port forward there is no address translation in the way. Anything listening on that port is directly exposed.
inbound_access.delete_pinhole_port_port_:
Delete the pinhole for port {port}?

The rule goes away entirely, along with its description.
inbound_access.forward_points_address_no: A forward points at an address, not at a device, so eero requires a DHCP reservation for the target. Any device can be chosen here and one will be reserved for it if it has none. Both sides accept a range, and both must cover the same number of ports, so the end of the internal range follows from the external one. Forwarding a port exposes that device to the internet.
inbound_access.inbound_rules_explained: Allows traffic from the internet to reach devices on your local network. Doing this weakens the firewall that would otherwise turn inbound traffic away, so choose your inbound rules carefully.
inbound_access.internal_range_runs_past_: That internal range runs past port 65535.
inbound_access.ipv4_forward_text: Redirects a port (or ports) on your public IPv4 address to specific devices on your local network.
inbound_access.ipv6_pinhole_text: Opens the firewall straight through to a device's own global address.
inbound_access.nothing_from_internet_can: Nothing from the internet can reach in.
inbound_access.one_port_low_high_range: One port, or a low-high range like 3478-3480
inbound_access.one_port_low_high_range_2: One port, or a low-high range like 3000-3002
inbound_access.opens_firewall_device_s_o: Opens the firewall to the device’s own address
inbound_access.pinhole_translates_nothin: A pinhole translates nothing, so the port is the same on both sides.
inbound_access.redirects_port_your_publi: Redirects a port on your public address
inbound_access.reservation_failed_first: The address could not be reserved, so no forward was created. {detail}
inbound_access.reservation_made_with_for: Port forwards require a reserved IP address, so we'll make one now.
inbound_access.set_external_range_both_m: Set by the external range: both must cover the same number of ports.
inbound_access.there_one_port_both_sides: There is one port on both sides of a pinhole, because nothing is being translated. eero keeps no description for one, so Eeronaut stores it for you.
insights.average_hour_across: An average hour, taken across {caption} in your own time zone — so a quiet column is a reliably quiet time rather than one idle evening. Useful for deciding when a large backup or a firmware update will bother nobody.
insights.average_traffic_by_hour_over: Average traffic by hour of the day over {caption}
insights.concentration_caption: {devices} clients account for {share}% of the traffic
insights.concentration_many: {devices} clients account for {share} of everything moved in {caption}, out of {of} seen.
insights.concentration_one: {devices} client accounts for {share} of everything moved in {caption}, out of {of} seen.
insights.download_from_each_speed_test: Download from each speed test, in Mbps, oldest first
insights.each_hour_last_day: Each hour of the last day on its own, in your own time zone. One day gives one reading per hour, so a quiet column here is one quiet hour rather than a habit — the 7d and 30d views average across days, which is what turns this into a pattern.
insights.heaviest_explained: Download and upload added together over {caption}, heaviest first, for the twelve busiest clients of the {count} eero saw in that window. The two charts above split the same window by direction, which is where to look when a client is heavy in only one of them.
insights.network_where_handful_clients_d: A network where a handful of clients dominate can behave very differently from one where the load is spread evenly. Worth keeping an eye on.
insights.no_download_recorded_window_try: No download recorded in this window. Try a longer period — a short one can fall between eero's reporting intervals.
insights.no_per_client_usage_window: No per-client usage in this window. eero attributes traffic to clients only while they are on the network, so a quiet period shows nothing.
insights.no_speed_tests_recorded_eero: No speed tests recorded. eero runs these on its own schedule; Run speed test above files one immediately.
insights.no_upload_recorded_window_try: No upload recorded in this window. Try a longer period — a short one can fall between eero's reporting intervals.
insights.nothing_sent_more_than_received: Nothing sent more than it received in this window.
insights.security_activity_threats_conte: Security activity — threats and content blocked, ad and tracker counts — is part of eero Plus. This network has no active subscription, so there is nothing to report here.
insights.traffic_hour_over_last_24: Traffic by hour over the last 24 hours
insights.upload_from_each_speed_test: Upload from each speed test, in Mbps, oldest first
insights.uploading_more_than_downloads_u: Most clients download more than they upload, but some devices (backup client, cameras sending footage, torrent boxes, etc) are the legitimate exception. Worth a look to ensure no surprises.

interrupt.bands: Every device on {bands} drops while the radios are paused
interrupt.guest: Interrupts your connection for about twenty seconds
interrupt.guest_reconnect: Guests disconnect and need the new password to rejoin

local_control.backup_internet_part_eero_: Backup internet is part of eero Plus. This network has no active subscription.
local_control.backup_intro: If your Internet connection ever goes down, you can configure a backup service to take over automatically.
local_control.cellular_standing_by: Standing by. It carries no traffic until the wired connection fails.
local_control.change_password_title: Change the password eero uses to join this network
local_control.hotspot_backup_part_eero_p: Hotspot backup is part of eero Plus, which this network does not have.
local_control.remove_ssid_backup_if_your:
Remove "{ssid}" as a backup?

If your main connection fails, the eeros will no longer fall back to it.
local_control.scan_taking_longer_than_ex: The scan is taking longer than expected. Anything it finds will appear here on the next visit.
local_control.takes_over_automatically_w: eero Signal kicks in at the first sign of a WAN outage. It's prioritized over any hotspot backups you may have configured below and will continue to operate until you hit your Signal data limit, or until the Signal device is removed from your network.
local_control.try_network_after_others: Try this network after the others
local_control.try_network_before_others: Try this network before the others
local_control.use_backup_connection_keep: Uses a nearby Wi-Fi connection to keep the network online during a wired outage. eero works down the list below in order.
login.eero_will_send_verification_code: eero will send a verification code. Your password is never used and never stored.
login.new_code_on_its_way: A new code is on its way.
login.session_encrypted_rest_anyone_acce: The session is encrypted at rest. Anyone with access to this server can use it, so leave it off on shared machines.
login.stay_signed_in: Stay signed in on this device
login.use_different_login: Use a different email or number
network.about_adguard: Run by AdGuard, which also makes ad-blocking software; its resolvers come in filtering and non-filtering flavors.
network.about_cloudflare: Cloudflare’s resolver, on the same global network as its CDN. It validates DNSSEC and does not pass client-subnet information on to authoritative servers.
network.about_comodo: A public resolver from the security vendor Comodo.
network.about_controld: Run by Control D, a DNS filtering company based in Toronto. Its free resolvers come unfiltered or with one of several blocklists.
network.about_google: Google’s public resolver, among the most used in the world. It validates DNSSEC and passes a client-subnet hint.
network.about_level3: Resolvers on the backbone once run by Level 3, now part of Lumen. Long-standing and widely used.
network.about_opendns: Cisco’s public resolver, independent as OpenDNS until Cisco bought it in 2015.
network.about_quad9: Run by the Quad9 Foundation, a Swiss non-profit, and best known for refusing to answer for domains tied to malware and phishing.
network.anything_holding_these_can_join: Anything holding these can join your Thread network.
network.bridge_mode_eeros_do_no: In bridge mode the eeros do no routing. There is nothing else to configure here.
network.bridge_mode_has_nothing_configur: Bridge mode has nothing to configure
network.bridged_unavailable: {what} is unavailable in bridge mode. The eeros are acting as access points and are not routing, so there is nothing here to configure.
network.changing_band_s_security_mode: Changing a band's security mode makes its clients reconnect. 6 GHz is fixed at WPA3 because the specification requires it.
network.confirm_automatic:
Switch to Automatic addressing?

Devices renew onto eero’s default range.
network.confirm_bridge:
Switch to Bridge mode?

The eeros become plain access points: DHCP, port forwards, reservations, and the firewall all stop applying, and another router has to hand out addresses. Devices will drop while it changes over.
network.confirm_delete_reservation:
Delete the reservation for {ip}?

That device will get a different address next time it reconnects.
network.confirm_manual:
Apply this manual IP range?

Every device renews onto the new subnet; anything with a static address outside the pool stops being reachable, including whatever you are using now.
network.confirm_security_mode:
Change {label} from {from} to {to}?

Every device on that band disconnects and rejoins. Anything that cannot do the new mode will not come back.
network.confirm_vlan_remove:
Remove the uplink VLAN tag?

This changes how the gateway talks to your provider. If it is wrong, the whole network loses internet access and this interface goes with it — the only way back is physical access to the gateway eero.
network.confirm_vlan_tag:
Tag the uplink with VLAN {tag}?

This changes how the gateway talks to your provider. If it is wrong, the whole network loses internet access and this interface goes with it — the only way back is physical access to the gateway eero. Only set this if your provider told you to, and use the number exactly as they gave it.
network.confirm_wan_change:
Change the internet connection to {mode}?

This is how the gateway gets its address from your provider. If it is wrong, the whole network loses internet access and the only way back is physical access to the gateway eero.
network.copies_these_credentials_into_ap: Copies these credentials into the Apple and Google keychains on phones running the eero app automatically.
network.dns_caching_hint: The eeros answer repeated lookups themselves instead of asking your resolver every time.
network.dns_locked_by_plus: eero Plus filters at eero's own resolver, so it will not let this network use a different one. Turn off every Plus filter — ad blocking and advanced security here, and content filters, SafeSearch, and blocked apps on each profile — and this comes back. One filter on one profile is enough to hold it.
network.eeros_bridge_mode_do_no: The eeros are in bridge mode and do no routing, so they hand out no resolvers. Whatever router is doing DHCP decides which DNS servers this network uses.
network.explain_dnssec: DNSSEC: answers are checked against their cryptographic signatures, so a forged or tampered reply is thrown away rather than trusted.
network.explain_ecs: ECS: part of your network’s address is passed on to the site’s own name servers, so they can point you at a server near you. Slightly faster, slightly less private.
network.explain_filtered: Filtered: the resolver refuses to answer for domains on a blocklist — malware and phishing hosts, and on some of these, ads or adult sites as well. A blocked name simply does not resolve, so nothing on the network can reach it.
network.guest_consequence: Your connection drops for about twenty seconds while the eeros apply the change. Nothing restarts. Continue?
network.guest_not_loaded: The guest network settings did not load. Reload the page to try again.
network.guest_off_disconnects: Anything connected to the guest network loses access immediately.
network.guest_security_follows_primary: The guest network runs on the same radios as the primary network and uses the same security mode. Change it above.
network.hand_dns_back_your_provider:
Hand DNS back to your provider?

Resolution moves to whatever servers your ISP advertises. Any filtering or blocking those custom resolvers were doing stops.
network.isp_dns_has_nothing_configure: ISP DNS has nothing to configure
network.issue_new_thread_network_key:
Issue a new Thread network key?

Every Thread accessory you own is joined with the current key and will stop working until you re-pair it by hand, one device at a time. There is no undo.
network.last_check_unpairs_every_thread: Last check: this unpairs every Thread accessory. Continue?
network.lets_applications_open_their_own: Lets devices and apps on your network automatically open and manage router ports they need for incoming connections, without you manually configuring port forwards.
network.lets_capable_clients_use_several: Lets capable Wi-Fi 7 devices use several bands at once for higher throughput, lower latency, and more reliable connections.
network.lets_much_older_clients_associat: Allows older Wi-Fi devices to connect, but may reduce overall wireless performance.
network.low_power_mesh_smart_home: The low-power mesh smart-home devices use, and what Matter accessories join over. Harmless to leave on.
network.lowers_power_draw_when_network: Lowers power usage by adjusting your gateway's Ethernet data rate based on your maximum internet speed.
network.mlo_enables_wpa3: WPA3 is enabled on the bands that take part, and some older devices cannot join an MLO network.
network.move_reservation_ip_device_keeps:
Move this reservation to {ip}?

The device keeps its current address until its lease renews, so the change may not take effect immediately.
network.name: Name
network.new_thread_credentials_issued_re: New Thread credentials issued. Re-pair your accessories.
network.no_password_to_reveal: This network has no password set, so there is nothing to reveal.
network.no_reservations_yet_reservation_: No reservations yet. A reservation pins a client to one address so a forward or a firewall rule keeps pointing at it after a reboot.
network.not_an_ip_address: That is not a valid IP address.
network.only_if_your_provider_requires: Only if your provider requires one. A wrong tag takes the connection down and cannot be undone from here.
network.outside_subnet: That address is outside this network's subnet ({cidr}).
network.own_dns_server_praise: It looks like you're running your own DNS server locally. Nice work, Smarty!
network.pause_bands_hint: Turns {bands} off for {minutes} minutes to allow older 2.4 GHz devices a chance to join if they're struggling to connect. eero restores the radios on its own, so there's no need to come back and switch it off later. Every device on {bands} drops to 2.4 GHz while this is enabled.
network.pause_bands_temporarily_every_de:
Pause {bands} for {minutes} minutes?

Every device on those bands moves to 2.4 GHz or drops while it lasts. eero restores them by itself when the time is up, but you can always switch it back on sooner yourself.
network.picking_device_fills_address_usi: Selecting a device fills in its current IP address, but you can change it if you'd like. A device with no address yet is offered one that nothing else is using.
network.power_saving_schedule_hint: Reduces energy use during scheduled times. Devices remain connected, but network performance is reduced.
network.randomizes_outbound_source_ports: Randomizes outbound source ports. Slightly better privacy; occasionally upsets strict-NAT games.
network.reduces_latency_under_load: Manages and prioritizes network traffic to reduce latency and keep connections responsive when your internet connection is busy.
network.requires_your_provider_offer_ipv: Requires your provider to offer IPv6. Turning it on without upstream support achieves nothing.
network.reservation_deletes_any_forward: Any port forward on that address will be deleted along with it.
network.reservation_needs_ip_address: A reservation needs an IP address.
network.resolution_handled_your_provider: With ISP DNS, resolution is handled by your provider: the eeros pass on whatever servers it advertises on the WAN link.
network.separate_ssid_visitors_isolated_: Creates a separate Wi-Fi network for visitors and devices you may not fully trust, keeping them isolated from devices on your main network.
network.service_plan_hint: The upload and download speeds included in your current internet service plan. Leave blank if unknown.
network.set_label_wpa3_only_devices:
Set {label} to WPA3 only?

Devices that cannot do WPA3 will stop being able to join this band. Most hardware more than a few years old cannot. "WPA2 and WPA3" accepts both and is usually what you want.
network.six_ghz_requires_wpa3: 6 GHz requires WPA3; the standard allows nothing else.
network.some_providers_need_username_pas: Some providers need a username and password to bring the link up. eero encrypts them against the gateway before storing them.
network.steers_clients_to_best_eero: Helps devices connect to the eero access point and band that should provide the fastest, most reliable connection. Some older clients roam badly with it on.
network.use_these_dns_servers_if:
Use these DNS servers?

If they are wrong or unreachable, name resolution stops for the whole network while the link stays up.
network.vlan_id_not_valid_enter: This VLAN ID is not valid. Enter a whole number between 1 and 4094.
network_switcher.cannot_tell_whether_net: Cannot tell whether this network is reachable from here
node_panel.confirm_reboot: Reboot {name}? Every client on it loses its connection for about two minutes. The rest of the network keeps working, and devices in range may move to another eero.
node_panel.confirm_reboot_gateway: Reboot {name}? This is your gateway, so the whole network goes down rather than just the clients on it, and it takes several minutes to come back.
node_panel.confirm_remove: Remove {name} from the network? Removing this eero may reduce coverage and cause connectivity issues in your eero network. Eeronaut cannot add it back — that has to be done from the eero app on Android or iOS, and it means setting the eero up again from scratch.
node_panel.could_not_read_nightlight_set: Could not read the nightlight settings.
node_panel.downward_lamp_beacon_separate: The downward lamp on a Beacon, separate from the small status light on the front.
node_panel.gateway_stays: The gateway cannot be removed — it holds the internet connection, and taking it off would leave no network to add it back through.
node_panel.light_failed: Could not change the status light.
node_panel.port_bridging: {count} devices reach the network through this port, so something is bridging them onto it. eero cannot see the switch itself.
node_panel.truemesh_hint: eeros do not use a fixed backhaul. Every eero links wirelessly to every other eero in range, on both 2.4 and 5 GHz, and eero's TrueMesh routing chooses which of those links to send traffic over — re-deciding as interference, congestion, and load change, and rerouting on its own if a node drops off. So this names the path in use at the moment the panel loaded, not a fixed parent. It is chosen for throughput and latency rather than for signal strength alone, so the nearest eero is not always the one picked.
node_panel.unreachable_alert: This eero cannot be reached over Ethernet or Wi-Fi. Check that it is plugged in, powered on, and still where you expect it to be.
node_state_help.connecting: This eero is joining the network: it has power and is talking to eero, but is not serving clients yet. If it stays here for more than a few minutes, check its link to the rest of the mesh.
node_state_help.issue: This eero's light is yellow: it is reachable but reports a problem, most often a weak or lost mesh link or an internet connection it cannot use. Open it for the detail eero gives.
node_state_help.restarting: This eero is restarting. Clients on it lose their connection until it is back, usually within about two minutes, and devices in range may move to another eero meanwhile.
node_state_help.signal_configuring: This eero Signal is setting itself up: scanning for a carrier, or applying a change to the one it uses. It cannot carry traffic until it finishes, which usually takes a few minutes.
node_state_help.signal_issue: {issue}. The Signal cannot carry traffic until this clears.
node_state_help.signal_no_reception: {issue}. Try repositioning your Signal or attaching it to a different eero device located elsewhere in your home.
node_state_help.signal_unregistered: This eero Signal has no cellular registration yet, so it cannot carry traffic if the wired connection drops. Registration usually completes on its own; if it does not, check the SIM and the plan in the eero app.
node_state_help.signal_updating: This eero Signal is installing firmware. It cannot carry traffic until the install finishes.
node_state_help.updating: This eero is installing a firmware update. It restarts when the install finishes, and clients on it lose their connection for a couple of minutes then.
nodes_overview.eero_reports_no_reboot_ti: eero reports no reboot time for this node. This is how long it has been connected to eero's cloud.
nodes_overview.eero_returned_no_nodes_ne: eero returned no nodes for this network. That normally means the cloud has not heard from the gateway recently rather than that the hardware is gone.
nodes_overview.reboot_time_cannot_be_rig: eero's record of when this eero last rebooted is older than the last firmware install, and installing firmware reboots every eero — so it cannot be right. This is how long the eero has been talking to eero's cloud instead.
profile_filters.ad_block_held_by_network: Turned on for every profile by {link}. eero will not let a profile opt out while that is set, so turn it off there first, then choose which profiles it applies to.
profile_filters.ad_blocking_off_profile: Ad blocking off for this profile.
profile_filters.ad_blocking_profile: Ad blocking on for this profile.
profile_filters.blocking_works_refusing_: Blocking works by refusing the service’s DNS names, so an app that talks to an IP address directly will still get through.
profile_filters.blocks_advertising_track: Blocks advertising and tracking domains at the DNS layer, for the devices in this profile only.
profile_filters.categories_apply_every_d: Categories apply to every device in this profile.
profile_filters.levels_identical: {levels} block exactly the same things, and eero does not record which was chosen, so either one leaves this profile filtered identically.
profile_filters.profile_s_filters_do_not: This profile’s filters do not match any preset. Pick one to start from, then change individual filters below.
profile_filters.recurring_window_when_pr: A recurring window when this profile loses internet access. Devices stay on the network and reconnect on their own when the window ends. Times are in your network’s timezone.
profile_filters.remove_all_length_schedu:
Remove all {length} scheduled pauses from {name}?

This profile will no longer pause on a schedule. Any pause currently in effect ends, and the windows cannot be recovered — they would have to be entered again.
profile_filters.sites_blocked_allowed_de: Sites blocked or allowed for the devices in this profile only. The Security tab keeps a separate network-wide list that applies to everyone; an allow here overrides a block from content filtering.
profile_filters.starting_point_sets_ever: A starting point that sets every filter below at once. Change any of them afterwards.
profiles.confirm_delete.one: Delete “{name}”? Its {count} device goes back to Unassigned.
profiles.confirm_delete.other: Delete “{name}”? Its {count} devices go back to Unassigned.
profiles.default_profile_cannot_deleted: The default profile cannot be deleted
profiles.devices_assigned_afterwards_fro: Devices are assigned afterwards, from the profile itself.
profiles.every_client_already_profile: Every client is already in this profile.
profiles.every_client_belongs: Every client belongs to exactly one profile. A client you have not put in a profile sits in {unassigned}, which eero creates on every network. Removing a client from a profile moves it back to Unassigned.
profiles.no_devices_assigned_profile: No devices assigned to this profile.
profiles.not_an_image: That file is not an image this browser can read.
profiles.nothing_restricted_profile: Nothing is restricted for this profile
profiles.nothing_scheduled_profile: Nothing is scheduled for this profile
profiles.photo_too_large: That image is too large. Choose one under 10 MB.
profiles.profile_groups_person_s_devices: A profile groups a person's devices so they can be paused together and filtered as a unit.
profiles.profile_paused_one_its_schedule: This profile is paused by one of its schedules
profiles.remove_all_length_devices_from:
Remove all {length} devices from {name}?

They stay on the network and keep working, but stop being covered by this profile's filters and schedules. Each one moves back to Unassigned, and they would have to be added again one at a time.
radio_analytics.airtime_used_each_radio_: Airtime used on each radio over time. Above roughly 60% is where a band starts to feel slow. A marked point is eero moving that radio to a new channel on its own.
radio_analytics.channel_change_line: Moved from channel {from} to channel {to} at {when}
radio_analytics.eero_keeps_this_long: eero keeps about {hours} hours of radio history, whatever window is asked for.
radio_analytics.no_radio_history_reporte: No radio history reported for this period.
radio_analytics.no_radios_on_this_band: No radio on this network reported history for that band.
radio_analytics.per_radio_airtime_histor: Per-radio airtime history is part of eero Plus. This network has no active subscription.
radio_channels.chart_caption: Each radio on {band}, drawn across the stretch of air it occupies. Arc height is the airtime that channel is using.
radio_channels.no_radios: eero reported no radio figures for this network.
radio_channels.note_24: Only channels 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap on 2.4 GHz, so two eeros on nearby channels compete for the same air. Two on the same channel compete hardest of all.
radio_channels.note_5: A wider channel is faster when the air is quiet and more fragile when it is not: 160 MHz covers a third of the band, so anything else in that stretch is in the way.
radio_channels.note_6: 6 GHz has room that the other two do not, which is why eero puts wide channels here. It carries less far through walls.
radio_channels.part_eero_plus: Per-radio channels and airtime are part of eero Plus, which this network does not have.
radio_channels.title: Radio channels
reboot.consequence: You will lose internet connectivity for five to eight minutes. Continue?
resolver.cloudflare-family: For Families: blocks malware and adult content
resolver.controld-social: Blocks ads, trackers, and social media
security.blocks_advertising_tracking_dom: Blocks advertising and tracking domains at the DNS layer for every profile at once.
security.blocks_domains_known_host_malwa: Blocks domains known to host malware, phishing, and command-and-control traffic at the DNS layer.
security.domain_rules_explained:
One domain per line.
{domain} already covers every subdomain, {sub} covers only that one, and a bare {tld} covers every .org domain. Wildcards are not supported, so there is no {wildcard}.
security.editing_lists_part_eero_plus: Editing these lists is part of eero Plus, which this network does not have.
security.nothing_allow_list_entries_here: Nothing is on the allow list. Entries here override a block — useful when a filter catches a domain you need.
security.nothing_blocked_network_wide_bl: Nothing is blocked network-wide. Blocks added here apply to every client, including guests.
security.nothing_stopped_window: Nothing was stopped in this window.
security.these_rules_apply_every_profile: These rules apply to every profile at once. Each profile also keeps its own list, on its own page, for rules that should not cover the whole network. Allowing a domain overrides a block from content filtering.
settings.admins_owner_only: Only the network's owner can invite an admin.
settings.confirm_cancel_all: Cancel every pending admin invite? Every link stops working straight away.
settings.confirm_cancel_invite: Cancel this invite? The link stops working straight away.
settings.could_not_save_notification_set: Could not save that notification setting.
settings.could_not_save_report_setting: Could not save the report setting.
settings.hide_all_features_which_only: Hide all features which are only available with eero Plus
settings.hide_features_your_hardware_fir: Hide features your hardware or firmware does not support
settings.hide_icons_indicate_which_featu: Hide icons that indicate which features are part of eero Plus
settings.hide_plus_features_hint: Removes all disabled eero Plus features from the interface entirely, for an ad-free experience.
settings.hide_plus_marks_hint: For when you've paid for eero Plus, but don't want to be reminded of it. Nothing is hidden, and every feature keeps working.
settings.installing_firmware_restarts_ev: Installing firmware restarts every eero, so this decides when the network will drop for several minutes.
settings.interface_has_its_own_password: Eeronaut has its own local password, separate from your eero account.
settings.invite_admin_hint: An admin can change this network's settings. They cannot remove the owner or hand the network to somebody else.
settings.invite_link_ready: Copy this link and send it to them. It works once, and it expires.
settings.least_8_characters_there_no: At least 8 characters. There is no recovery path: if you forget it, the only way back in is to delete the data volume and start again. Changing it signs out every other browser.
settings.link_not_copied: Could not reach the clipboard. Select the link and copy it.
settings.network_nickname_hint: A label for this network, separate from its Wi-Fi name.
settings.off_default_because_knowing_cap: Off by default, because knowing a capability needs newer hardware or a firmware update is usually worth seeing.
settings.password_changed_any_other_brow: Password changed. Any other browser signed in here has been signed out.
settings.simple_setup_hint_off: New eeros wait to be added in eero's phone app. Turn this on and one connected by cable sets itself up instead; over Wi-Fi it still needs the app, because an eero is provisioned over Bluetooth.
settings.simple_setup_hint_on: A new eero connected by cable sets itself up, with no need to open eero's phone app. One joining over Wi-Fi still needs that app, because an eero is provisioned over Bluetooth.
settings.some_features_unavailable_given: Some features may be unavailable on a given network, due to either a subscription requirement or hardware limitations. You can control how these features are shown within Eeronaut's menus.
settings.time_zone_drives_schedules: Power-saving windows and usage charts are worked out in this zone, so changing it moves them.
settings.two_new_passwords_do_not: The two new passwords do not match.
signal_panel.keeps_network_online_over_c: Keeps the network online over cellular if the wired connection drops. Standing by is the healthy state — a Signal carrying traffic means the wired connection has failed.
speed_test.measuring: eero is measuring the link. Until this run finishes, the readings shown are from the previous one.
wan.auth_failed.blame: The credentials this connection presented were rejected.
wan.auth_failed.next1: Re-enter the PPPoE username and password under Network.
wan.auth_failed.next2: Confirm with your ISP that the account is active and not suspended.
wan.dns_unreachable.blame: Name servers are configured and not answering, so pages fail while the connection itself is fine.
wan.dns_unreachable.next1: Try a different DNS server — 1.1.1.1 or 9.9.9.9 works as a test.
wan.dns_unreachable.short: Connected, but DNS is not responding
wan.gateway_unreachable.blame: The default gateway is set but never replies. Nothing here will fix this — the fault is upstream of your eeros.
wan.gateway_unreachable.next1: Check the modem’s own status lights for a service alarm.
wan.gateway_unreachable.next2: Contact your ISP; everything on the eero’s side is already correct.
wan.gateway_unreachable.short: Your ISP’s router is not answering
wan.no_dns.blame: The connection is up and no DNS servers were handed out, so no name will resolve.
wan.no_dns.next1: Set a DNS server by hand, or power-cycle the modem to pick up your ISP’s.
wan.no_dns.short: Connected, but with no name servers
wan.no_gateway.blame: There is an IP address but no default gateway, so nothing can leave the network.
wan.no_gateway.next2: If this eero is bridged behind another router, check that router’s WAN side.
wan.no_gateway.short: An address, but no way out
wan.no_ip.blame: The cable is up and nothing upstream has handed out an IP address.
wan.no_ip.next1: Power-cycle the modem: many hold one lease for the first device they see.
wan.no_ip.next2: If your ISP needs PPPoE or a VLAN tag, set it under Network.
wan.no_ip.next3: If the modem was swapped recently, your ISP may still be registering it.
wan.no_ip.short: Connected to the modem, but with no address
wan.no_link.blame: The gateway eero sees no Ethernet carrier at all. This is the cable or the modem, not your ISP.
wan.no_link.next1: Reseat the cable at both ends, at the eero and at the modem.
wan.no_link.next2: Power-cycle the modem and give its own lights time to settle.
wan.no_link.next3: Try another cable, or the modem’s other Ethernet port.
wan.no_link.short: Nothing is connected to the WAN port
wan.unknown.blame: No WAN state came back on this poll, so there is nothing to diagnose yet.
wan.unknown.next1: Check again in a moment; if it stays blank, make sure the gateway eero is reachable.
wan.walled.blame: Traffic is being intercepted by a captive portal before it reaches the internet.
wan.walled.next1: Open any http:// page from a device on this network and finish the sign-in.
wan.walled.next2: On hotel or campus links, the portal often has to be re-done after a reboot.
wan.walled.short: Something upstream wants you to sign in
wan_diagnosis.connection_came_back: The connection came back. The rest of the app should work again.
wan_diagnosis.reads_gateway_directly: This reads the gateway eero directly, so it needs this machine to be on the same network as the eeros, though not the internet.
